articles.title: Houthi missile strike on Yemen camp kills 73 security recruits, local authorities say

events.summary: A Houthi missile strike hit a government-controlled training camp in Yemen's Shabwa province. The attack killed 73 security recruits, according to local authorities.
events.why: A mass-casualty strike on military recruits threatens regional stability and could trigger severe escalations in the Yemeni conflict.

articles.title: Ukraine says it carried out first drone airlift of wounded soldier from front line

events.summary: Ukraine's military announced it conducted its first drone airlift to evacuate a wounded soldier from the front line. Ground extraction was impossible due to surrounding landmines and enemy drones.
events.why: The successful medical evacuation by drone represents a major technological precedent in battlefield logistics and combat casualty care.

articles.title: Exiled critic of Rwandan president found beheaded

events.summary: Former Rwandan army sergeant major Robert Kabera, an exiled critic of Rwanda's president, was found beheaded. He was a popular YouTuber and singer who had sought asylum in Uganda.
events.why: The murder of an exiled dissident in a neighboring country points to transnational repression and risks escalating regional political tensions.

articles.title: Deadly fire at Canada military base moved a kilometre 'in 30 to 60 seconds'

events.summary: A rapid fire at a Canadian military base advanced one kilometer in under a minute. The blaze killed four men and injured dozens of others.
events.why: A fatal disaster at a military facility raises serious concerns about base safety protocols and emergency management.

articles.title: US church on front line of battle against drug known as 'tranq'

events.summary: A US church is actively responding to the proliferation of the drug known as 'tranq'. The drug landscape has shifted due to a plentiful supply of potent synthetic opioids like fentanyl.
events.why: The spread of new adulterants in synthetic opioids intensifies the public health crisis surrounding overdose fatalities.

articles.title: Clean up begins after French riots but police remain

events.summary: Clean-up operations began across France following widespread riots, with police remaining deployed. In Marseille alone, over 600 shops were reported looted.
events.why: Mass unrest and property destruction inflict substantial economic costs and test state stability and public security.

articles.title: Watch: Shops looted and restaurants gutted in Paris riots

events.summary: More than half a million people demonstrated across France over the weekend amid widespread violence. The unrest resulted in looted shops and gutted restaurants in Paris and other cities.
events.why: Large-scale civil unrest across an entire nation poses critical challenges to national governance, economic activity, and public safety.

articles.title: Ex-OpenAI worker accused of planting bug had Saudi support, claims prosecutors

events.summary: Abdulrahman Alfozan, a former OpenAI employee accused of planting a recording device, was denied bail. Prosecutors allege he acted with Saudi state support.
events.why: Allegations of state-sponsored corporate espionage targeting leading AI firms have significant implications for international espionage and national security policy.

articles.title: Huge setback for Alberta's separatist movement after decisive defeat

events.summary: Alberta's separatist movement suffered a decisive electoral defeat. Although leadership has pledged to continue, the significant margin of defeat poses a major setback.
events.why: A decisive defeat alters the trajectory of regional separatist politics in Canada and eases immediate constitutional challenges.
